newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WESTERN CAPE UPS ROLE IN S.AFRICAN ECONOMY - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: WESTERN CAPE UPS ROLE IN S.AFRICAN ECONOMY - REPORT.

text.p: The Western Cape is increasing its role in the South African economy, upping its gross geographic product (GGP) share by 0.9 percent between 1988 and 1994, the Bureau of Market Research (BMR) said on Wednesday.
"The Western Cape's share in the gross geographic product increased by 0.9 percent (between 1988 and 1994) from 13.2 percent to 14.1 percent," the University of South Africa's BMR said in a report.
It said the Gauteng and Northern Province increased their share by 0.6 percent while the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal showed a marginal increase of 0.1 percent each in their share.
In contrast, the contribution of the North-West and the Free State to total production decreased by 1.2 percent ond 0.9 percent respectively.
A slight decrease was also evident in Mpumalanga (down 0.2 percent) and the Northern Cape (down 0.1 percent).

Turning to average annual growth (at constant 1990 prices) of GGP in each province between 1988 and 1994, the BMR said the North-West, Free State and the Northern Cape registered negative growth rates.
"The highest positive growth rates were experienced in the Northern Province with 3.2 percent and the Western Cape with 1.3 percent," it said.
The other four provinces registered growth rates of less than 1.0 percent.

The BMR said sectoral structure also exhibited changes with the primary sector (agriculture, fishing, mining and quarrying) showing a decline of almost five percentage points in its contribution to the South African economy.
The share of the secondary sector (especially trade and catering, including tourism, finance and real estate) showed substantial increases in their contribution to the economy.
According to the BMR, these changes could be largely attributed to the variations in sectoral growth rates.
"Between 1988 and 1994 negative growth rates were experienced in the manufacturing sector (-1.2 percent) and the mining sector (-0.5 percent).

The bureau said all other sectors showed positive growth rates with electricity and water (up 2.7 percent), transport and communication (1.6 percent), construction (1.3 percent), community services including government services (1.3 percent) and financial and real estate (1.0 percent) the best performers.
